subject: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@atlasapps.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasapps.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the test plan we discussed so we’re all aligned:

Call summary (2 min)
- AtlasApps goal: reduce chat latency variability for user-facing assistant while keeping token cost within current budget. You want a head-to-head against the hyperscaler endpoint you already use (SkyForge AI) and a Redwood-configured baseline.
- Key workload: multi-turn chat (average prompt ~120 tokens, final responses 40–150 tokens), occasional long-context retrieval-driven prompts up to 2,048 tokens.

Competitive angles you care about
- p95 and p99 tail latency (critical)
- sustained tokens/sec under steady concurrent sessions (throughput)
- cold vs warm startup behavior (first-request penalty)
- model fidelity parity (we’ll run small prompt quality checks)

Proposed A/B probe matrix (short):
- Latency buckets: short (prompt+response ~32 tokens), medium (~160 tokens), long (~1024 tokens). Measure p50/p95/p99 for each.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under 16, 64, 128 concurrent contexts (sustained).
- Warm vs cold: 100 single-shot cold starts, then sustained stream for 30 minutes.
- Quantization/variant check: float32 vs int8/4 variants where relevant.

Deliverables and owners
- Redwood will provide: test harness (Docker + small readme), a spreadsheet matrix with test permutations, and an initial run on our Dedicated infra for comparison. Attachment: redwood-vs-skyforge-matrix.xlsx (first draft). — Owner: Monica (we agreed she’ll assemble).
- AtlasApps will provide: representative prompt set (10–15 prompts per length bucket) and a representative concurrency profile. — Owner: Evan/Priya.
- Timeline: aim to kick off lab tests next week (target start Mon 2029-07-08), 3–5 business days for runs and initial readout.

Security/confidentiality
- Per your ask, we’ll treat results as mutually confidential during evaluation; happy to sign an NDA if legal needs it.

Open questions for you (quick)
1) Any specific p99 target you consider a make/break?
2) Do you want us to include any of your internal routing/failover scenarios in the probe (we can simulate region failover)?

Next steps
- Evan: share prompt set and any throughput traces by EOD Tue (2029-07-02).
- Monica: upload final test harness + matrix and confirm exact model variants by Wed.
- Markus: provision Dedicated pool for the runs and provide estimated cost differential.

Thanks — I’ll update the Google folder and attach the matrix draft now.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-vs-skyforge-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub with test permutations)

From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@atlasapps.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasapps.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan

Thanks Jasmine — this looks good and matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

• p99 target: we’re currently seeing ~850ms p99 on SkyForge for our medium prompts; anything under ~600–650ms would be compelling.
• We’ll provide the prompt set and a heatmap of our concurrent session distribution.
• NDA: legal prefers a short mutual NDA before significant data exchange; I’ll loop them in if needed.

We’re fine with the proposed start window next week — team will confirm final availability tomorrow.

Evan
Evan Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasApps
evan.torres@atlasapps.com | (212) 555-0121

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan

On Sun, Jun 30, 2029 at 3:12 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> (call recap...)

Looks good. Quick ops notes from my side:
- I’ll reserve a small Dedicated pool (2 x A100-equivalent) for dry runs and a larger pool (burst up to 6 GPUs) for the main throughput sweep.
- Cost note: the main sweep (multi-variant) will require a short reserved window; I’ll send an estimated cost delta by EOD Tue.
- Can we pin the model to our q8_0 variant for one arm and fp16 for the other to surface quantization impact? That will give a clean signal on tokens/sec vs latency tradeoff.

Monica — please confirm the harness can run both SkyForge and Redwood endpoints side-by-side (we have a simple adapter already). If not, prioritize that adapter so we can run simultaneous A/B.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan

Markus / Jasmine — attaching the current test matrix and a short readme for the harness. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAtlasProbe

Attachment: test-harness-readme.md (contains docker run commands, env vars for endpoint URLs, and the adapter README)

Planned test steps (high level):
1) Sanity: run 50 short prompts against both endpoints to validate correctness and warm caches.
2) Latency sweep: per-length p50/p95/p99 for 1000 requests each length bucket (short/medium/long).
3) Throughput sweep: sustained 30-minute runs at concurrency levels 16, 64, 128 measuring tokens/sec and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Cold-start: 100 cold single-shot requests separated by 30s intervals.
5) Variant runs: fp16 vs q8_0 vs int8 (if supported) to capture quantization impact.

Open items for Jasmine/Evan:
- Confirm exact tokenization assumptions (we’ll use tiktoken-cl100k as baseline unless you specify otherwise).
- Confirm any additional failure modes to simulate (region failover, auth throttling).

I’ll tag the spreadsheet cells with the specific commands and expected CSV outputs. Once Evan shares the prompt set we can populate and kick off.

— Monica

From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@atlasapps.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasapps.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2029 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: AtlasApps competitive probe & p95/p99 A/B plan

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Confirming:
- We’ll share 12 prompts across short/medium/long buckets by EOD Tue (2029-07-02).
- NDA: I’ll have legal send over a mutual NDA; once that’s in place we can share a larger set and some live traces.
- Start date: target Mon 2029-07-08 looks good on our side.

Please proceed with the harness and matrix updates; once Monica marks the matrix final we’ll hand over the prompt pack.

Evan
